articles.title: Notes first: the plain habit that later becomes an agent's memory | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: Keep notes as plain files and a second reader can use them. What the app adds — conventions and computed views — is what a tool has to reconstruct. A check of what survives when the app is gone.

articles.title: PHP2Shell: When a Flaw in the Runtime Goes from Zero to Millions of Attacks | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: PHP2Shell affected roughly 70% of the web. The patch exists — but fixing a runtime flaw means the hosting provider has to act, not the site builder.

articles.title: What a Playtest Actually Gives Away | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: A studio shrank a playtest over AI cloning fears. What the public record shows about build leaks, clip-to-lookalike copies, and the limits of hiding a build.

articles.title: Flint: a Laptop Coding Model Built by AI | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: Recursive says its Eureka Machine built Flint, an open-weight local coding model, and that Flint tops its class. What is verifiable — and how close is "AI builds AI" really?

articles.title: When an AI Agent Acts for You: What Meta's Muse Revealed About Authorization | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: Meta's Muse shared a seller's address, gave a confused answer about reading his messages, and made "private" share links findable. What the first weeks reveal about agent permissions.

articles.title: What a 0.93 Actually Means | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: OpenAI's Decisions API returns a confidence with every choice. The numbers rank cases well — but they run optimistic, and how optimistic depends on what you ask the model to decide.

articles.title: What the MicroDuck Actually Gives You for $399 | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: The viral Microduck is a real open-source robot trained in simulation. The product holds up; the 20,000-preorder, NVIDIA-company, and Christmas-delivery claims do not.

articles.title: What Does OpenAI's Aurora Image-Model Testing Actually Establish? | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: OpenAI's API briefly listed three aurora image models in October 2026 and then published nothing about them. What the testing reports actually establish - and what they don't - is the story.

articles.title: What did DeepSeek actually open-source? | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: DeepSeek open-sourced the real inference engine — but not the cache, routing, and retention machinery behind its published revenue figures, and the margin headlines carry a correction trail.

articles.title: October's Deep Dive: Models: Promises and Breakthroughs | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: Thirteen launches in twenty-six days, each one a bundle of claims. What October's model releases actually established — and the checklist for what you can inspect a month on.

articles.title: When your desktop agent reports to your phone: What Tencent WorkBuddy's remote control and MCP ERP bridge actually wire together | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: Tencent's WorkBuddy connects mobile messaging to an unlocked office desktop and bridges that desktop directly to enterprise ERP systems via MCP. Bypassing the friction of the desk also removes the exact window where human supervision lived.

articles.title: The model isn't the agent: what a ten-harness comparison actually shows | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: Ten coding harnesses, one open model, the same 113 DeepSWE tasks: solved counts spanned 62 to 3. What that vendor-run comparison shows — and how to read any coding-agent benchmark.

articles.title: The test changed. What did the score mean? | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: A leaderboard score fell from 55 to 46 with no model update. Two archived page captures show every one of its evaluation scores stayed identical while the index around them was rebuilt — and what that means for any ranking you read.

articles.title: What does an AI lab's compute bill commit it to? | Orange Tomato
articles.excerpt: Anthropic S-1/A pairs $33.2B in nine-month revenue with about $417B in minimum compute obligations — and the filing itself separates a firm floor, a cancelable cap, and estimates it excludes. What each promise is, and what it is not.

series.title: Obsidian: from notes to agents
series.description: Five pieces on what a personal note vault has to be before an agent can work over it, and what each stage makes possible that the one before it could not. Each piece stands alone; read in order, they follow one question from a folder of notes to several agents sharing one memory.
series.note: Later slot titles are working titles until the piece ships.
